graph.title: LEGO City Ambulance 4431

new_part_types.name: Steering wheel on 1x2 plate (black wheel, yellow plate; inventory label 9553)
Wheel holder 2x2 with one pin (light grey)
Traffic light pole with base (light grey)
Brick 1x1 black with side stud (traffic light)

notes: Element IDs come from the inventory pages (pp. 66-67). Many are not in the catalogue, so new part types were drafted. Their port lists are simplified (generic stud / anti-stud, plus hinge/pin where obvious).

Two inventory labels, 9342 (red minifig legs, x2) and 9553 (steering wheel on plate, x1), are not valid element IDs, and the catalogue stand-ins lego-970c00 and lego-9566 were also rejected. The red legs b4/b11 now use the generic catalogue type lego-minifig-legs (colour=red). The steering wheel b89 uses a new descriptively named type lego-steering-wheel-on-plate. The original inventory labels are kept in the part labels.

Counts: 300901 (brick 1x6 white) is 6 and 663601 (tile 1x6 white) is 8, as on the parts page. The extra 300901 are b191-b193 and the extra 663601 are b194-b197. Their stud positions are inferred because the step pictures are small.
Stickers (star of life, licence plate, ambulance lettering) are not parts and are omitted.
Most stud edges between repeated pieces (red 1x4 plates, white 1x6 bricks, light grey 1x2 bricks) are plausible rather than read exactly from the pictures. Per-ID piece counts are what I matched.

Uncertain assignments: 4537987 (white bracket piece, placed at the cab pillar), 4527637 (stretcher pad), 4222017 (medic case body), 4211658 and 4211881 (stretcher IV arm and wheel holders), 4527947 (cab roof plate). The dark-red lights 3005741 and 3000841 are also uncertain: two on the rear roof, two as ends of the rear light row, one on the traffic light and one on the bike.

Connectivity: the booklet builds the ambulance, the street scene (pavement, bin, hydrant, traffic light) and the bicycle as separate small models, and the minifigs and stretcher separately. The graph links them with contact edges only: paramedics hold the stretcher, the driver sits in the seat, the man stands by the bike, the bike leans on the pavement, and the ambulance's first tire touches the pavement as in the cover scene. Those contact links are display arrangements and not fastened joins. No joined edge crosses between models.
Wheels are a repeat of 4 (hub 4211764 + tire 4568644) attached to the four wheel holders b28, b29, b34, b35 via attach overrides. The contact edge to 'wheel1.tire' refers to the first expanded copy.

The rear door pivots on the black hinge plates b119/b120. The roof hatch pivots on the red clip pieces b121/b122. The catalogue has no named hinge ports for those red pieces, so their ports are left null.

graph_initial.title: LEGO City Ambulance 4431

new_part_types.name: Wheel holder 2x2 with one pin (light grey)
Traffic light pole with base (light grey)
Brick 1x1 black with side stud (traffic light)

notes: Element IDs are taken from the inventory pages (pp. 66-67). Many are not in the catalogue, so new part types were drafted; port lists for these are simplified (generic stud / anti-stud, plus hinge/pin where obvious).

The booklet has two numbered bags: bag 1 (paramedics, stretcher and the ambulance body up to step 24) and bag 2 (cab, hatch, rear door, wheels, traffic-light/street scene, bicycle). All are in one graph.
Stickers (star of life, licence plate, ambulance lettering) are not parts and are omitted.

Step pictures are small and several pieces are hard to identify. Inventory counts were matched exactly (each Element ID appears the listed number of times), but which stud a piece joins is partly inferred. Stacked-piece edges are therefore approximate for repeated pieces (e.g. red 1x4 plates, white 1x6 bricks, light grey 1x2 bricks).

Uncertain assignments: 4537987 (white bracket piece, placed at the cab pillar), 4527637 (stretcher pad), 4222017 (medic case body), 4211658 and 4211881 (stretcher IV arm and wheel holders), 4527947 (cab roof plate), 3005741/3000841 dark-red lights (two on the rear roof, two as ends of the rear light row, one each on traffic light and bike).
The four wheel assemblies (hub 4211764 + tire 4568644) are a repeat attached to the four wheel holders b28, b29, b34, b35 via overrides.
The rear door pivots on the black hinge plates b119/b120. The roof hatch pivots on the red clip pieces b121/b122; the ports for these are not named in the catalogue so they are left null.

The two paramedics and the man are built from pieces separately from the ambulance; paramedic cases are held in the hand (contact edges). The stretcher is placed in the rear (contact edge). The driver paramedic sits on the driver seat (contact).
